# aeneid-091 — drafter's notes (XII.1–106)

55 units, 106 lines; paragraphs at 1, 18, 54, 81 carry `p`. Script checks print only the count line.
No set piece from the conventions list falls here; no new house renderings; no advisory (the battle talk
and Turnus's threat to foul Aeneas's hair are words, not described violence; Amata's death is only foreshadowed).

## Misprints (rule 5b: t as printed, l/i corrected, note opens "The print has X, a misprint for Y, corrected here.")
- **12.45 `dividit. ”Haudquaquam`** — the QUESTIONS 82 pattern (fifth case after 10.451, 11.98, 11.827, 11.849).
  t of unit 43 ends `dividit.`, t of unit 45 begins `”Haudquaquam`; l/i close Latinus's speech after
  *dividit.*; EXEMPT = {43, 45}; both notes open with the print's reading.
- **12.52 lower-case `longe`** after the full stop ending 51: misprint for *Longe* (item 43 practice). The stop
  itself is fine (Turnus's boast ends, the sneer at Venus begins); unit cut at `sanguis.` as printed.
- **12.60 `recumbit).` + lower-case `unum`**: misprint for a comma. *per has… lacrimas, per… honos* needs a verb
  and has it in *oro*. Cut does not break the sense: 56–60 runs on across the stop to `oro:` (exactly five lines).
- **12.81 `recessit.` + lower-case `poscit`**: misprint for a comma; *Haec ubi dicta dedit… recessit* is a *ubi*
  clause whose main verb is *poscit*. 81–84 is one unit to `auras.` (four lines), running across the stop.
- **12.89 `cristae.` + lower-case `ensem`**: misprint for a comma; *ensem* (90) takes up *ensemque* (89) in
  apposition. Unit 88–91 (`simul aptat… unda.`) runs across the stop.
  For 60/81/89 the precedent is aeneid-019 (*clipeum.* / *magni*), 020 (391) and 063 (626): unit runs on, l/i
  read the comma. No unit boundary had to be put at a misplaced stop.

## Variants noted for sense (kept as printed)
- **12.55 `monitura`** (LL `moritura`). Greenough's *monitura* construes ("meaning to warn/counsel him"); the
  Latin Library's *moritura* ("resolved to die") is, from memory, the reading of most modern texts and fits
  62–63. Not treated as a misprint (both construe; doubtful). Reviewer: if you judge it a misprint, only the
  note's opening and l/i of unit 54 change.
- **12.104 `atque`** (LL `aut`): noted briefly in unit 103 (lines 103–106) (sense hardly changes).
- Orthographic variants (inpavidus, adcenso, lacrumis, adscire, volnere, quoi, voltus, adstabat, Exin/exim)
  are glossed as Greenough's spellings where the word is discussed; *siquis* not remarked.

## Doubts for the reviewer
- 53 (unit 52) `sese occulat`: taken as the goddess hiding herself (grammatical subject); some take it loosely of Aeneas.
- 46 `aegrescitque medendo` l "sickens with the healing", i "grows worse for being treated" — check for echo of a
  known version (I avoided "the cure").
- 25 (unit 24) *nec genus indecores*: *genus* as accusative of respect — check.
- 79 *et Rutuli* taken as a loose second subject of *quiescant* (nominative plural).
- 72 *Ne… prosequere* called 'ne' + present imperative of the deponent.
- From memory, unchecked: XI.434–444 (Turnus's promise), XI.115–118 (Aeneas's offer of single combat),
  VII.96–101 (Faunus's oracle), Turnus as Amata's sister's son (Venilia), Iliad XX.164–175 (Achilles as lion),
  V.311–345 (Aphrodite and Apollo rescue Aeneas), IV.141–147 (ivory stained with purple), VI.487–489, XIX.400–403,
  XVIII.205–214; Georgics III (the training bull, c. 232–234); Iarbas's *semiviro comitatu* (IV.215);
  Pilumnus as Turnus's ancestor (grandfather at X.76?, not stated in the note).
- Elision lists in the notes were made by eye; please check.

## Lines for hand scansion (packet flags none)
- **12** *ignavi Aeneadae*, **63** *generum Aenean* — elision onto Ae-; Ae- one long syllable.
- **60** *Teucris*, **78** *Teucros… Teucrum* — eu one syllable.
- **17, 80** *coniunx*; **66** *subiecit* — consonantal i after prefix.
- **40** *consanguinei* — five syllables (con-san-gui-ne-i, gu consonantal); check the scanner does not merge -ei.
- **83** *Orithyia* — line-end *dedit Orithyia*; check syllabification (Ō-rī-thyi-a with -yia as two?).
- **84** *anteirent* — -ei- by synizesis (an-tei-rent, three syllables): *qui candore nives anteirent, cursibus auras*.
- **87** *dehinc* — two syllables here (Ipse de|hinc…); the scanner may prefer one.
- **65** *quoi* — one long syllable (= cui).
- **59** *in te omnis* — elision of the monosyllable *te*.
- **64, 17, 80** *Lavinia* — Lā-, four syllables.
